title: Brought into the hearing chamber at Carthage
english: In the second consulship of Praesens, with Claudianus as his colleague, on 17 July, Speratus, Nartzalus, and Cittinus were brought into the hearing chamber at Carthage, and with them Donata, Secunda, and Vestia.
translator_notes: The Latin names the consul Claudianus, and the reading text keeps the printed name. Gebhardt's apparatus gives Condiano (Usener), and the historical consuls of AD 180 are Praesens II and Condianus; the printed Claudiano is likely a scribal form. The variant is recorded in the source file. XVI kalendas Augustas is 17 July.

title: We have done no wrong
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "You can earn the pardon of our lord the emperor if you come back to your right mind." Speratus said: "We have never done wrong. We have had no part in wickedness. We have never cursed anyone; when we were ill-treated, we gave thanks. That is why we revere our Emperor."

title: Our religion is simple, says the proconsul
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "We too are devout, and our religion is simple. We swear by the genius of our lord the emperor, and we pray for his well-being. You must do the same."

title: The mystery of simplicity
english: Speratus said: "If you will give me a quiet hearing, I will tell you the mystery of simplicity."

title: Swear by the emperor's genius
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "I will not listen while you begin to speak evil of our sacred rites. Swear instead by the genius of our lord the emperor."

title: I serve the God no eye has seen
english: Speratus said: "I do not acknowledge the empire of this age. Rather, I serve that God, whom no human being has seen, or can see, with these eyes. I have never stolen. If I buy anything, I pay the tax, because I know my Lord and Emperor, the ruler of the kings of all nations."

title: The evil persuasion is murder and false witness
english: Saturninus the proconsul said to the others: "Give up this persuasion of yours." Speratus said: "The evil persuasion is to commit murder and to bear false witness."

title: No one else to fear
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "Do not take part in this madness." Cittinus said: "We have no one else to fear, only the Lord our God, who is in heaven."

title: Honour to Caesar, fear to God
english: Donata said: "Honour to Caesar, as Caesar's due; but fear to God." Vestia said: "I am a Christian." Secunda said: "What I am, that I want to remain."

title: Do you persist in being a Christian?
english: Saturninus the proconsul said to Speratus: "Do you persist in being a Christian?" Speratus said: "I am a Christian." And all the others agreed with him.

title: Nothing to think over in a just cause
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "Do you want time to think it over?" Speratus said: "In a cause so just, there is nothing to think over."

title: Books, and letters of Paul
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "What are the things in your case?" Speratus said: "Books, and letters of Paul, a righteous man."

title: Thirty days to reconsider, refused
english: Saturninus the proconsul said: "Take thirty days, and think it over." Speratus said again: "I am a Christian." And all the others agreed with him.

title: The sentence read from the tablet
english: Saturninus the proconsul read the decree from the tablet: "Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Donata, Vestia, Secunda, and the rest have confessed that they live by the Christian rite. They were given the chance to return to the Roman way, and they obstinately held fast. It is therefore ordered that they be punished with the sword."

title: Today we are martyrs in heaven
english: Speratus said: "We give thanks to God." Nartzalus said: "Today we are martyrs in heaven; thanks be to God."

title: The names proclaimed by the herald
english: Saturninus the proconsul ordered the herald to proclaim: "Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Veturius, Felix, Aquilinus, Laetantius, Ianuaria, Generosa, Vestia, Donata, and Secunda: I have ordered them to be led away."
translator_notes: The herald's list names twelve, six more than the six brought in at the hearing (Veturius, Felix, Aquilinus, Laetantius, Ianuaria, Generosa). The Latin is translated as printed; the extra names are not explained in the text.

title: Beheaded for the name of Christ
english: All of them together said: "We give thanks to God." And at once they were beheaded for the name of Christ.
